headline: Foggy mornings and mild sunny afternoons continue through Thursday, then a front brings wind and light rain Friday into Saturday, with cooler air after.
summary: As of Tuesday evening, western Washington stays mild through Thursday. Each night and morning brings low cloud and fog, with the densest fog in the north and south interior and around the Olympics. Fog was already thickening Tuesday evening, with visibility down to a quarter mile in spots, especially around Mukilteo. Forecasters are watching overnight conditions and may issue a fog advisory. Fog should clear by early afternoon Wednesday, leaving sunny afternoons. Thursday morning fog is much less likely, though a few valleys could still see some. Highs warm slowly through Thursday, with a few spots reaching the low 70s. Overnight lows run from the upper 40s to the low 50s, with light northwest winds around 5 to 10 mph. A weather system arrives later Friday and continues through Saturday. Winds pick up across the area ahead of it on Friday, with stronger winds and rough seas on the coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Rain should be light, about a tenth to a quarter of an inch through late Saturday. Colder air follows this weekend and into early next week. Any leftover showers could leave light snow on the mountains above roughly 4,500 feet. Foothills and outlying areas could see lows in the 30s, so frost is possible early next week, though forecasters say confidence in that is not high and no frost headline has been issued. Confidence is fairly good in the mild, foggy-morning pattern through Thursday. About 60 to 70 percent of computer model runs show a fairly deep trough (a dip in the jet stream) moving through with Friday's system, so details of that system remain somewhat uncertain. No official watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for western Washington land areas.
changes: Early forecasts called for light rain Friday into Saturday and mentioned no wind or cold. By afternoon, forecasters added a Friday front with wind, a rainfall estimate of about a tenth to a quarter inch, and cooler weather with possible frost early next week. By evening, the focus shifted to dense fog tonight, with a fog advisory possible.
